blocks.h2: What a Skokie Plumbing Inspection Covers

steps.body: Age, draft, relief valve and sediment.
Galvanized pipe, pressure and valves that work.
Slow drains and signs of root problems.
Sump and ejector pumps tested with water.

blocks.intro: Skokie's population grew from about 15,000 in 1950 to nearly 60,000 in 1960. Thousands of homes got their plumbing at once.

items.body: Pipe, valves and sewer laterals installed in the same decade wear out together.
Threaded galvanized joints are where leaks start.
A checkup helps you budget for a repipe or a sewer repair.

blocks.h2: Plumbing Maintenance Questions From Skokie Homeowners

items.q: Is a yearly checkup worth it for an older home?
items.answer: Yes. In a home where most of the plumbing is original, catching a small leak or a weak valve early saves money.

items.q: Can you tell me if I need to repipe?
items.preview: Yes, after we look at the pipe and pressure.
items.answer: Yes. We check the type and condition of your supply pipe and the water pressure, and we'll tell you honestly.

items.q: Does the No Drip Club include checkups?
items.answer: The [No Drip Club](/no-drip-club) includes regular maintenance visits.

items.q: Can you inspect before I sell?
items.answer: Yes. Fixing small issues before listing helps the buyer's inspection go smoothly.

items.q: What fails first in a 1950s Skokie home?
items.preview: Often the sewer line and old valves.
items.answer: Often the sewer lateral, old shutoff valves and galvanized pipe.

items.q: Can you check my water heater's venting?
items.answer: Yes. We test the draft to make sure exhaust goes up the chimney.

items.q: How much does plumbing maintenance cost in Skokie?
items.preview: It depends on the visit. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on what's included. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
